subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A flood hydrograph with a short lag time and high peak discharge usually indicates:
options: A rapid flashy response, e.g. urban or impermeable basin
A gentle slow response, e.g. forested basin
questions.explain: A short lag time and high peak show water reaching the river quickly, raising flood risk.

questions.q: The flat area either side of a river that floods and is built up by deposited sediment is the:
questions.explain: A floodplain is the wide, flat valley floor built up by sediment left behind when the river floods.

questions.q: A river generally has its greatest discharge and carries its largest total load in its:
questions.explain: By the lower course, tributaries have added water, so discharge and total load are greatest.

questions.q: On the outside of a meander bend, the river mainly:
options: Deposits sediment forming a slip-off slope
Erodes, forming a steep river cliff
questions.explain: Faster flow on the outer bend erodes the bank, creating a river cliff.

questions.q: A wave-cut notch is formed at the:
options: Base of a cliff where waves erode a hollow
questions.explain: Waves erode a hollow at the cliff base called a wave-cut notch, undercutting the cliff above.

questions.q: A wave-cut platform is formed as:
options: Sediment is deposited at a river mouth
A stack collapses into a stump
A cliff retreats, leaving a rocky surface at its base
questions.explain: As waves undercut and the cliff retreats, a flat rocky platform is left at the base.

questions.q: Why does deforestation in a drainage basin increase flood risk?
options: Less interception and infiltration means water reaches the river faster
questions.explain: Removing trees cuts interception and infiltration, so rain runs quickly into the river, raising flood risk.

questions.q: Groynes are wooden or rock barriers built out into the sea in order to:
options: Trap sediment and build up the beach
questions.explain: Groynes interrupt longshore drift, trapping sediment to widen the beach.

questions.q: On a flood hydrograph, the 'lag time' is the gap between:
questions.explain: Lag time is the delay between the heaviest rainfall and the river reaching its highest discharge.

questions.q: When rocks knock together and become smaller and rounder, the process is:
questions.explain: Attrition wears rocks down as they collide, making them smaller and rounder.

questions.q: The breaking down of rock in place (without movement) by weather, plants or chemicals is called:
questions.explain: Weathering breaks rock down in situ, unlike erosion which also wears away and removes it.

questions.q: Natural raised banks of sediment along the edges of a river channel are called:
questions.explain: Levees are raised banks built up by repeated deposition during floods.

questions.q: Erosion caused by the sheer force of fast-moving water hitting and pushing into cracks in the bank is called:
questions.explain: Hydraulic action is the force of water compressing air in cracks, weakening rock.

questions.q: Dissolved minerals carried invisibly in the water are transported by:
questions.explain: In solution, dissolved load is carried chemically within the water.

questions.q: Longshore drift is the process that:
options: Transports sediment ALONG the coast in a zig-zag motion
questions.explain: Longshore drift moves sediment along the coast as swash arrives at an angle and backwash returns straight down.

questions.q: Managed retreat (coastal realignment) involves:
options: Allowing low-value land to flood and the coastline to move back
questions.explain: Managed retreat lets the sea flood low-value land, creating natural defences like salt marsh.

questions.q: A long ridge of sand or shingle joined to the land at one end and projecting into the sea is a:
questions.explain: A spit is a depositional ridge attached to the coast at one end, formed by longshore drift.

questions.q: Which sequence shows the correct order in which erosional landforms develop on a headland?
questions.explain: A crack becomes a cave, then an arch, then a stack when the arch collapses, then a stump.

questions.q: Freeze-thaw weathering on a cliff happens when:
options: Water in cracks freezes, expands and widens the rock until pieces break off
questions.explain: Repeated freezing and expanding of water in cracks widens them until fragments shatter off.

questions.q: On the INSIDE of a meander bend, where the water is slower, the river usually:
options: Deposits sediment forming a slip-off slope (point bar)
questions.explain: Slower flow on the inner bend deposits sediment, building a gently sloping point bar.

questions.q: Which is an example of HARD engineering river flood management?
options: Allowing the river to flood washland
Building a concrete dam and reservoir
questions.explain: Dams and reservoirs are hard engineering structures that control river flow.

questions.q: The point where a tributary joins the main river is called the:
questions.explain: A confluence is the point where a tributary meets the main river channel.
